newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks stable, New Toyo disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks stable, New Toyo disappoints.

text.p: Singapore shares were mostly stable in light early Friday trade.
At 0215 GMT, the benchmarket Straits Times Industrials Index was up 0.07 points at 2,078.15. Turnover was just 22.4 million shares, with 103 losers against 57 gainers.
New Toyo bounced to $0.85 on its debut but then fell back to S$0.785, 1.5 cents below its initial public offer price in a sign that retail fever for new issues is fading, dealers said.
Most of the volume came from blocked deals. NatSteel saw 750,000 of its 815,000 shares crossed at S$3.58 while Delifrance saw 783,000 of its shares crossed at S$1.48.
Property-linked Hong Fok, active with over 1.2 million shares traded, was up S$0.13 at S$2.63.
Creative's expectations of better earnings in the third quarter ended March 31 1997 pushed its shares up a staggering S$1.80 to S$15.40. Volume was around 155,000 shares.
Singapore Telecommunications recovered from yesterday's 18-month low to trade around S$2.87, up six cents.
Activity on Malaysian shares traded over the counter remained cautious after yesterday's sharp fall. The UOB OTC index was down 3.25 points at 1,227.12.
